AcceptedOut.description: The answer to a request that is carried out later, by the worker.
AcceptedOut.title: AcceptedOut

AdHocTarget.description: Typed messages, sent the same for every item (the item's input is not used).
AdHocTarget.title: AdHocTarget

BudgetAction.description: What an exhausted budget does: notify its channels, or also block gateway calls.
BudgetAction.title: BudgetAction

BudgetPatch.description: A partial edit: the fields sent replace the budget's. Send `scope_id` with `scope`.
BudgetPatch.title: BudgetPatch

BudgetPeriod.description: The UTC calendar period a budget's spend is summed over before it starts again.
BudgetPeriod.title: BudgetPeriod

BudgetScope.description: Whose spend a budget caps. Every scope but `project` names one value in `scope_id`.
BudgetScope.title: BudgetScope

BudgetSpec.description: A whole budget: the body of a create.
BudgetSpec.title: BudgetSpec

BudgetStateOut.description:
Where the budget stands in the current period (by the server's clock).

Until the first evaluation of a new period, the previous period's figures no longer apply:
the state shows the current period with `spent_usd` null and `state` `ok` (a firing alert
from a past period ends on that evaluation and never blocks).
BudgetStateOut.title: BudgetStateOut

ChannelCreate.description:
A new channel. `config` and `secret` are validated for the `kind` sent with them.

Slack and PagerDuty need `secret` (the incoming-webhook URL, the routing key); email and
webhook channels refuse it. An omitted `config` is the kind's default, which only Slack and
PagerDuty have. Errors come out under `config.<field>` and `secret`.
ChannelCreate.title: ChannelCreate

ChannelUpdate.description:
A partial edit: only the fields sent change. A channel's kind never changes.

`config` is validated against the channel's kind (`parse_config`), so it is taken as an
object here. `secret` replaces a Slack URL or PagerDuty routing key; `rotate_secret`
generates a new webhook signing secret, returned once.
ChannelUpdate.title: ChannelUpdate

CompletedScore.description: One score a reviewer gives; exactly one of `value` and `string_value`.
CompletedScore.title: CompletedScore

Completion.description: The body of a complete: one score per config of the queue.
Completion.title: Completion

CredentialCreate.description: A new provider credential. `base_url` is only for `openai_compatible`, which needs it.
CredentialCreate.title: CredentialCreate

DatasetItemIn.description: One item to store. `input` is required and may be any JSON except null.
DatasetItemIn.title: DatasetItemIn

DatasetPatch.description: The body that edits a dataset; only the description changes. `null` clears it.
DatasetPatch.title: DatasetPatch

DatasetSpec.description: The body that creates a dataset.
DatasetSpec.title: DatasetSpec

DayStats.description:
One UTC day of one user. A day without traces is all zeros with a `cost_usd` of 0; a day
with calls but none priced has `cost_usd` `None`.
DayStats.title: DayStats

Delta.description: `b - a`, and that as a fraction of `a` (`None` when `a` is 0).
Delta.title: Delta

DetectorRunOut.description: One run of one detector. `findings` is `None` when the run failed (`error` is set).
DetectorRunOut.title: DetectorRunOut

EmailConfig.description: Who gets the email: 1 to 10 addresses, stored lower-cased and without repeats.
EmailConfig.title: EmailConfig

EvalResultOut.description: What the evaluator would score; nothing is stored. `cost_usd` is the call's real cost.
EvalResultOut.title: EvalResultOut

EvaluatorBudgetOut.description:
A judge's budget and its UTC calendar month so far; `reserved_usd` is held by running
calls.
EvaluatorBudgetOut.title: EvaluatorBudgetOut

EvaluatorBudgetStatusOut.description: The month so far (UTC calendar month). `remaining_usd` counts reservations as spent.
EvaluatorBudgetStatusOut.title: EvaluatorBudgetStatusOut

EvaluatorFilters.description: Which traces online sampling considers. Empty lists match everything.
EvaluatorFilters.title: EvaluatorFilters

EvaluatorOut.description: An evaluator. `budget` is `null` for an evaluator without a monthly budget.
EvaluatorOut.title: EvaluatorOut

EvaluatorPatch.description:
The members to change; absent ones stay. `config` holds only the config fields to change
and may not change `kind`; a judge's `judge_template` replaces its `prompt_version_id`.
`monthly_budget_usd: null` clears the budget (refused for judges).
EvaluatorPatch.title: EvaluatorPatch

EvaluatorRunOut.description:
One evaluation. `source` is why it ran (`online`, `test` or `experiment`); `cost_usd` is
what the run is charged (zero until it settles); `reserved_usd` what a running judge call
holds against the budget; `scores` the scores it wrote (empty until it is done).
EvaluatorRunOut.title: EvaluatorRunOut

EvaluatorSpec.description: A whole evaluator: the body of a create.
EvaluatorSpec.title: EvaluatorSpec

EvidenceOut.description: The traces and numbers behind an insight; decimals are strings, unknown values `None`.
EvidenceOut.title: EvidenceOut

ExperimentSpec.description: The body that creates an experiment.
ExperimentSpec.title: ExperimentSpec

ExplanationOut.description:
Claude's explanation of an insight: plain text, advisory, and what the call cost.

`cost_usd` is the call's cost from its token usage (the reserved worst case when the answer
reported no usage).
ExplanationOut.title: ExplanationOut

ExportFilters.description: The trace-list filters. `from` and `to` are required and at most 90 days apart.
ExportFilters.title: ExportFilters

FallbackCondition.description: A failure after which the gateway moves on to the route's next target.
FallbackCondition.title: FallbackCondition

FallbackPolicy.description: The failures after which the gateway tries the next target. Empty means never.
FallbackPolicy.title: FallbackPolicy

FaultProfileCreate.description: A new fault profile. Omitted `params` are the scenario's defaults.
FaultProfileCreate.title: FaultProfileCreate

FaultProfileUpdate.description:
A partial edit: only the fields sent change.

`params` must be sent with `scenario` (they are only meaningful together); a `scenario`
sent without `params` resets the params to that scenario's defaults. `expires_at` is cleared
by sending `null`; every other field must have a value when it is sent. `changes()` tells an
absent field from one sent as `null`.
FaultProfileUpdate.title: FaultProfileUpdate

FaultScenario.description: A failure the gateway can inject (the Integration Lab); each has its own params.
FaultScenario.title: FaultScenario

GatewayKeyCreate.description:
A new gateway key. Without `route_id` it uses the project's default route.

A `None` limit means no limit; a `None` `cache_ttl_seconds` leaves the cache off.
GatewayKeyCreate.title: GatewayKeyCreate

GatewayKeyUpdate.description:
A partial edit: only the fields sent change.

The four nullable settings (`rpm_limit`, `tpm_limit`, `cache_ttl_seconds`, `fault_profile_id`)
are cleared by sending `null`; every other field must have a value when it is sent.
`changes()` tells an absent field from one sent as `null`.
GatewayKeyUpdate.title: GatewayKeyUpdate

GatewayOverviewOut.description:
Gateway traffic of a window of at most 7 days.

`errors` includes calls failed on purpose by Lab faults; `faults` says how many of the
requests carried one. `fallbacks` and `retries` are event counts, not request counts: the
switches to another target, and the repeated tries on one target, summed over all requests.
A latency is `null` when no request measured it.
GatewayOverviewOut.title: GatewayOverviewOut

HealthComponentOut.description:
One source of penalty. `observed` and `baseline` are decimal strings, `None` when unknown
(or when the component has no baseline: findings and errors).
HealthComponentOut.title: HealthComponentOut

HealthOut.description:
The health score over the window; `value` is `None` (never 0) when it had no LLM calls.

`approximate` is true when a percentile behind the score was estimated from rollup histograms.
HealthOut.title: HealthOut

InsightDetailOut.description: The insight and its completed explanations, newest first.
InsightDetailOut.title: InsightDetailOut

InsightSummaryOut.description: Counts of the insights that still need a person: `open` and `acknowledged` ones.
InsightSummaryOut.title: InsightSummaryOut

InvitePreviewOut.description: What an invite grants, shown to the signed-in invitee before they accept.
InvitePreviewOut.title: InvitePreviewOut

ItemPatch.description: The body that edits an item: the fields sent change, `null` clears `expected_output`.
ItemPatch.title: ItemPatch

ItemsIn.description: Traces to queue; `span_id` queues that span of each trace instead of the whole trace.
ItemsIn.title: ItemsIn

JudgeConfigIn.description:
A judge config as a request sends it: a prompt version of the project, or one of the
built-in judge templates (`app.evals.judge_templates`), exactly one of them. The service
turns a template into the project's prompt `judges/<name>` version 1 and stores the version
id, so a stored judge always names a prompt version (`JudgeConfig`).
JudgeConfigIn.title: JudgeConfigIn

LastRunOut.description: An experiment's latest run, for its list row.
LastRunOut.title: LastRunOut

LoginSignedInOut.description: The password (or the second step) was enough: the session cookies are set.
LoginSignedInOut.title: LoginSignedInOut

LoginTotpRequiredOut.description:
The password was right but the account has two-factor authentication: no cookies yet.

Send `challenge` with a code to `POST /auth/totp/verify` before `expires_at`.
LoginTotpRequiredOut.title: LoginTotpRequiredOut

MalformedJsonParams.description: A 200 whose body is cut to `keep_fraction` of its length; non-streaming calls only.
MalformedJsonParams.title: MalformedJsonParams

MessagesSource.description: Messages typed in the playground, sent as they are.
MessagesSource.title: MessagesSource

ModelAdvice.description: Free-form advice for clients on how to run the prompt; the server never uses it.
ModelAdvice.title: ModelAdvice

ModelShare.description: A model's share of each release's LLM calls (`None`: that release made no calls).
ModelShare.title: ModelShare

NewError.description: A normalised failure message that spans of `b` have and spans of `a` do not.
NewError.title: NewError

OAuthIdentityOut.description: A sign-in provider account linked to the caller.
OAuthIdentityOut.title: OAuthIdentityOut

OrgUpdateIn.description:
A change to the organization: any of its fields, and at least one.

A field that is left out is left alone; `null` is not a way to say that, so it is refused.
Strict about unknown fields, so a client that sends one this route does not handle is told
instead of being answered 200 with nothing changed.
OrgUpdateIn.title: OrgUpdateIn

PagerDutyConfig.description: The severity PagerDuty shows on events from this channel.
PagerDutyConfig.title: PagerDutyConfig

Params.description: Sampling parameters; an unset one is left to the provider's default.
Params.title: Params

PlaygroundConfig.description: One run: a credential of the organization, a model, parameters and what to send.
PlaygroundConfig.title: PlaygroundConfig

PlaygroundResultOut.description: One configuration's run, in the order of the request. `error` set means no `output`.
PlaygroundResultOut.title: PlaygroundResultOut

PromptCreate.description: The body of `POST /prompts`: the prompt and its version 1.
PromptCreate.title: PromptCreate

PromptSource.description: A stored prompt version with the values of its variables.
PromptSource.title: PromptSource

PromptVersionByIdOut.description:
The version with its prompt's name. The model advice is `model_config` on the wire and
`advice` in code, because pydantic reserves the name.
PromptVersionByIdOut.title: PromptVersionByIdOut

PromptVersionTarget.description: A stored prompt version; each item's input fills its variables.
PromptVersionTarget.title: PromptVersionTarget

QueueSpec.description: The body of a queue create.
QueueSpec.title: QueueSpec

ReleaseStats.description:
One release over a window. Unknown values are `None`, never 0.

`cost_usd` is the sum of the priced spans: `None` only when nothing was priced, and a lower
bound while `unpriced_calls` is above 0.
ReleaseStats.title: ReleaseStats

RetryPolicy.description:
How often a target is tried, the first try included, and how long to wait in between.

The wait before retry *n* is `min(backoff_ms * 2 ** (n - 1), max_backoff_ms)`, replaced by a
provider's `Retry-After` when `honour_retry_after` is set.
RetryPolicy.title: RetryPolicy

RouteConfig.description:
Which credentials serve the route's calls, in fallback order, and how failures are handled.

`timeout_ms` is the whole budget for every attempt, wait and fallback of one call; for a
stream it bounds the time to the first byte.
RouteConfig.title: RouteConfig

RouteUpdateIn.description: A new config, and the version the client last read, which must still be the current one.
RouteUpdateIn.title: RouteUpdateIn

RuleDefinition.description: What a rule measures and when it breaches. The preview's body.
RuleDefinition.title: RuleDefinition

RuleSpec.description:
A whole rule as a person writes it: the body of a create and of an edit.

An edit sends the whole rule again and replaces it; the rule's kind may change.
RuleSpec.title: RuleSpec

RunScoreOut.description:
A score a run wrote: `value` for numeric and boolean (1/0) scores, `string_value` for
categorical ones.
RunScoreOut.title: RunScoreOut

RunStart.description: The optional body that starts a run.
RunStart.title: RunStart

ScoreConfigPatch.description:
A partial edit: the fields sent replace the config's. The name cannot change; the type
can only while no score uses the name.
ScoreConfigPatch.title: ScoreConfigPatch

ScoreConfigSpec.description: A whole score config: the body of a create.
ScoreConfigSpec.title: ScoreConfigSpec

ScoreCreate.description:
A score a person adds to a trace on the dashboard. Send exactly one of `value` (a number,
or `true`/`false`) and `string_value`. `id` makes a retry idempotent.
ScoreCreate.title: ScoreCreate

ScoreDataType.description: What a score's value is: a number, one of a list of strings, or yes/no stored as 1/0.
ScoreDataType.title: ScoreDataType

ScoreSource.description: Who wrote a score: an API key, a person in the dashboard, or an evaluator.
ScoreSource.title: ScoreSource

ScoreSummaryOut.description: A trace's latest score of one name, as the trace list shows it.
ScoreSummaryOut.title: ScoreSummaryOut

SlackConfig.description: Nothing to configure: the incoming-webhook URL is the channel's secret.
SlackConfig.title: SlackConfig

SlowResponseParams.description: The first byte of the response delayed by `delay_ms`.
SlowResponseParams.title: SlowResponseParams

StatsWindow.description: The window the figures cover: the requested one widened to whole UTC days.
StatsWindow.title: StatsWindow

Target.description: One provider credential the route can send a call to.
Target.title: Target

TargetOverride.description:
Run a prompt-version experiment with another version of the same prompt; the credential
and model stay the experiment's.
TargetOverride.title: TargetOverride

TimeoutParams.description: The call held for `hold_ms`, or what is left of the route's budget, then timed out.
TimeoutParams.title: TimeoutParams

TotpEnabledOut.description: The recovery codes, in clear text this once: the server keeps only their hashes.
TotpEnabledOut.title: TotpEnabledOut

TotpSetupOut.description: What to add to an authenticator app. Returned once; the secret is never shown again.
TotpSetupOut.title: TotpSetupOut

TruncatedStreamParams.description: A stream closed after `after_chunks` frames, without its end marker.
TruncatedStreamParams.title: TruncatedStreamParams

UnsupportedParameterParams.description: 400 naming `param` as unsupported by the model.
UnsupportedParameterParams.title: UnsupportedParameterParams

UserStats.description:
One end user over the days of the window that have any activity.

`cost_usd` is the sum of the priced calls: `None` when calls were made and none was priced,
and a lower bound while `unpriced_calls` (the calls without a price) is above 0.
`first_seen_day` and `last_seen_day` are the first and last of those days. `errors` counts
failed LLM calls; the `error_count` of a session counts failed spans of every kind.
UserStats.title: UserStats

VersionUsageOut.description:
Over the last 7 days. `cost_usd` and `p95_ms` are null when unknown, never 0.

`cost_usd` sums the calls that have a cost; when `has_unpriced` is true some LLM calls had
none (unknown model or missing usage), so it is a lower bound.
VersionUsageOut.title: VersionUsageOut

WebhookConfig.description: Where the signed POST goes. The URL rules that need settings or DNS are in `urls.py`.
WebhookConfig.title: WebhookConfig

post.description:
Verify an address with the token from the emailed link.

No session is needed: the link is often opened in a browser that is not signed in, and the
token alone proves the inbox. Unknown, used, expired and wrong-kind tokens all answer the
same 404.
Send the signed-in user a fresh verification link, at most 3 per hour.

Check the password. A user with two-factor authentication gets a challenge, not a session.

The challenge is issued only after everything a session needs has held (throttle, password,
a password that is still current), so it means exactly "the first step passed".

schema.title: Response Login Api V1 Auth Login Post

get.description:
The caller's account and memberships: for a browser session, and for a personal access token.

This is the one `/auth` route a token may call, so a tool can check that its token works and
whose it is.

schema.title: Response List Identities Api V1 Auth Oauth Identities Get

get.description: The providers that can be used to sign in, so the login page shows only working buttons.

schema.title: Response List Providers Api V1 Auth Oauth Providers Get

delete.description: Unlink a provider account. The provider need not still be configured.

get.description:
Finish a sign-in or link, then redirect: to `next` on success, to an error page if not.

Every query parameter is optional so a callback that is wrong in any way still gets the
redirect the user can read, not a JSON validation error.

302.description: Redirect to `next` (with session cookies for a sign-in), or to `/login?error=<CODE>` (to `next` with `error=<CODE>` for a link). Clears `spl_oauth`.

get.description: Send the browser to the provider. `intent=link` links it to the signed-in user instead.

302.description: Redirect to the provider's sign-in page; sets `spl_oauth`.

post.description:
Email a reset link if the address has an account. The answer never says whether it does.

A known and an unknown address take the same path and get the same response: both are
counted by the limits first, and neither is turned away early. The only difference is that
a known address also gets a token and a queued email. The demo account counts as unknown.

Set a new password with the token from the emailed link.

No session is needed (the person forgot their password) and none is created: they sign in
afterwards with the new password. Every session of the account is ended. Unknown, used,
expired and wrong-kind tokens all answer the same 404.

delete.description: Sign out everywhere else: end every session of the user except the one making the call.

schema.title: Response List Sessions Api V1 Auth Sessions Get

get.description: The caller's tokens that can still be used. Never includes a secret.

schema.title: Response List Tokens Api V1 Auth Tokens Get

post.description: Create a token. The 201 is the only time its secret is shown.

delete.description: Revoke a token. Repeating it is fine; a token that is not the caller's is a 404.

post.description: Turn it off. Needs a valid code (TOTP or recovery), which is spent.
Turn it on with a code from the app. Returns the recovery codes, this once.
Make a secret for an authenticator app. Replaces one from an earlier, unconfirmed setup.

The second step of signing in: a challenge and a code make a session.

The user row is locked before the failure count is read, so concurrent attempts for one
account run one after another: the limit is exact, and a code cannot be spent twice. Wrong
codes are recorded as failed sign-ins, so they share the password's limit. A challenge issued
before the password changed is refused: it passed the first step against a password that no
longer exists.

get.description:
Show the org and role an invite grants, without accepting it.

Requires a signed-in user (the invitee), like accepting does. Unknown, used and expired
tokens all get the same 404, so the endpoint does not reveal which invites exist.

delete.description:
Delete the organization with its projects, traces, keys, members, invites and audit log.

Only an owner may, and only by typing the organization's slug as `confirm`. Everything goes
in one transaction: it is all deleted or none of it is. This is synchronous, which is fine for
the size of organization this runs; a very large one needs a background job.

patch.description:
Rename the organization, or require (or stop requiring) two-factor authentication.

`name` needs `org:update` (admins and owners) and `require_2fa` needs `org:security` (owners);
a request with both needs both, and is refused whole. Only values that change are applied and
audited, in one `org.update` event, so repeating a request is a no-op.

get.description: By name. Never includes a secret.

schema.title: Response List Channels Api V1 Orgs  Org Id  Alert Channels Get

delete.description: Rules that name the channel keep its id and skip it until they are edited.

patch.description:
Change the name, config or secret. The kind never changes.

`rotate_secret` (webhooks only) generates a new signing secret, returned once. A new config
or secret clears `verified_at`. Errors as for the create.

get.description: Newest first. `status` keeps `pending`, `sent` or `failed` deliveries.

post.description:
Queue a failed delivery again, with the same id, so receivers still deduplicate on it.

Its attempts start over and the worker picks it up at once; the last error stays until the
next attempt. `409 NOT_RETRYABLE` unless the delivery is `failed`.

Deliver a test now. A failing channel is a `200` with `status: "failed"` and the error.

`pending` when a failure a retry might fix left it to the worker. `sent` records the channel
as verified. At most 10 tests per channel an hour (`429 RATE_LIMITED`). An email channel
while no email provider is configured is `409 NOT_CONFIGURED`.

parameters.description: Makes a retry of this request safe: it runs once, then is replayed.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

schema.description: Makes a retry of this request safe: it runs once, then is replayed.
schema.title: Idempotency-Key

get.description:
The audit log, filtered like `GET /orgs/{org_id}/audit`, streamed as CSV (newest first).

A log with more than 50 000 matching events is refused before anything is sent.
get.summary: Download the audit log as CSV

get.description: Newest first. Never includes a key.

schema.title: Response List Credentials Api V1 Orgs  Org Id  Credentials Get

post.description:
Seal and store the key. `base_url` is required for `openai_compatible`, refused otherwise.

`409 NOT_CONFIGURED` without CREDENTIALS_KEYS; `422` on `base_url` for a URL that is not
`https://`, has userinfo, a query or a fragment, or resolves to a private address.

delete.description: `409 CREDENTIAL_IN_USE` while a gateway route sends calls through it.

post.description:
List the provider's models with the key and record the outcome as the last check.

A failing key is a `200` with `status: "error"` and a short reason such as `401 Unauthorized`.
Seal a new key in place of the old one. Clears the last check, which was of the old key.

schema.title: Response List Invites Api V1 Orgs  Org Id  Invites Get

post.description:
Create an invite and return its link; with an `email` and a sender, also mail it.

The invite, its audit event and the queued email commit in one transaction. Mailing only
changes how the link reaches someone: the invite is still accepted by any signed-in holder
of the link, whatever address it was mailed to.

schema.title: Response List Members Api V1 Orgs  Org Id  Members Get

get.description: Ordered by provider, pattern, start time and tier.

schema.title: Response List Price Overrides Api V1 Orgs  Org Id  Price Overrides Get

post.description:
Rates are USD per million tokens. `effective_from` defaults to now.

The pattern matches a model exactly or with a snapshot suffix, like the seed prices. The
optional cache-write rates fall back to the input rate; `min_prompt_tokens` (default 0) makes
the override one tier of the model, applied to prompts of at least that many tokens.
`409 PRICE_OVERRIDE_EXISTS` when the organization already has one for the same provider,
pattern, start time and tier.

delete.description: Spans ingested from now on fall back to the next price; stored costs are not rewritten.

schema.title: Response List Projects Api V1 Orgs  Org Id  Projects Get

get.description: The price table the server computes costs from. Any signed-in user, session or token.

schema.title: Response Get Prices Api V1 Prices Get

delete.description:
Delete the project with its traces, spans and API keys.

Admins and owners may, by typing the project's slug as `confirm`. The org's audit log keeps a
`project.delete` event with the name and slug, written in the same transaction.

get.description: Newest first. `state=firing` keeps open events, `state=resolved` resolved ones.

post.description: Record that you have seen the event. `409 ALREADY_ACKNOWLEDGED` the second time.

get.description: Firing rules first, then by name. Unpaginated: a project has at most 100 rules.

schema.title: Response List Rules Api V1 Projects  Project Id  Alert Rules Get

post.description:
Store a rule. `422 UNKNOWN_CHANNEL` for a channel outside the organization; `422
LIMIT_EXCEEDED` past 100 rules (budgets' rules do not count).

What the rule would have measured over the last 7 days, one point per window (at least
an hour apart, at most 168 points), with its line at each point.

Reads only; at most 30 previews per person a minute (`429 RATE_LIMITED`).

delete.description:
Delete the rule with its state and events. A firing alert is resolved first and sends
`alert.resolved`. Notifications already queued still go out.

patch.description:
Replace the rule with the whole rule sent; its kind may change. Errors as for the create.

Changing what a firing rule measures or judges, or disabling it, resolves its alert first
and sends `alert.resolved`; renaming it or changing its channels or cooldown does not.

post.description:
Stop the rule's notifications until `until` (at most 30 days ahead); `null` unmutes.

A muted rule still fires, resolves and records its events.

get.description: Newest first, each with its progress.

post.description: Store an empty queue. `409 NAME_TAKEN`, `422 UNKNOWN_SCORE_CONFIG`.

delete.description: Delete the queue with its items; the scores already given stay.

post.description:
The lowest-id pending item that is free, already yours, or claimed over 30 minutes ago;
`204` when there is none.

get.description: By id, oldest first; `status` keeps one status.

post.description: Queue up to 200 traces, or the given span of each. A trace already queued is skipped.

Score the item's trace: one score for each of the queue's configs, no others.
`409 ITEM_NOT_ASSIGNED_TO_YOU`, `422 SCORE_NOT_IN_QUEUE`, `422 SCORE_REQUIRED`.
Give your claimed item back to the queue. `409 ITEM_NOT_ASSIGNED_TO_YOU`.
Mark your claimed item skipped. `409 ITEM_NOT_ASSIGNED_TO_YOU`.

get.description: By name. Unpaginated: a project has at most 50 budgets.

schema.title: Response List Budgets Api V1 Projects  Project Id  Budgets Get

post.description:
Store a budget. `409 BUDGET_NAME_TAKEN`; `422 UNKNOWN_SCOPE` for a gateway key outside
the project; `422 UNKNOWN_CHANNEL`; `422 LIMIT_EXCEEDED` past 50 budgets.

delete.description:
Delete the budget with its alert history. A firing budget is resolved first and sends
`alert.resolved`; a blocking one stops blocking at once.

patch.description:
Change the fields sent; send `scope_id` together with `scope`. Errors as for the create.

Changing the amount, scope or period of a firing budget, or disabling it, resolves its alert
first and sends `alert.resolved`. A new scope or period clears the spend shown until the next
evaluation, about a minute later.

get.description: Newest first. `name` returns the dataset of that exact name, if any.

post.description: Store an empty dataset. `409 NAME_TAKEN`.

delete.description: Delete the dataset with its items. `409 DATASET_IN_USE` while an experiment uses it.

get.description: By id, oldest first.

post.description: Add up to 1 000 items. `422 DATASET_FULL` past 10 000 items; nothing is stored then.

Copy one item from each of up to 200 traces: the span `span_id`, else the trace's first
`llm` span. A trace that gives no item is listed in `rejected` with the reason (`trace not
found`, `no llm span`, `no payload stored`). The recorded output is only a starting point for
the expected output.

post.description:
Run 1 to 3 configurations at once and answer with one result each, in order.

A configuration that fails (a provider error, a missing variable) has its `error` and does
not affect the others; a project budget that blocks a call is `error = "BUDGET_EXCEEDED"`.
Responses are not streamed, so `ttft_ms` is null. `404` for a credential outside the
organization or a prompt version outside the project; `409 NOT_CONFIGURED` without the
gateway runtime or `CREDENTIALS_KEYS`; `429 RATE_LIMITED` after 30 runs a minute per user.
